dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: When multiplying by nines, invoke Ekanyūnena Pūrveṇa — 'By One Less than the Previous One'! Lessen the multiplicand by 1 for the left part, then subtract that from the nines for the right part.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>When multiplying by nines, invoke Ekanyunena Purvena — By One Less than the Previous One! Lessen the multiplicand by 1 for the left part, then subtract that from the nines for the right part.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Watch closely! For 47 × 99: lessen 47 by 1 to get 46 on the left. Then subtract from nines: 99 − 46 gives 53 on the right. Put them together: 4653!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Watch closely! For 47 times 99: lessen 47 by 1 to get 46 on the left. Then 99 minus 46 gives 53 on the right. Put them together: 4653!</prosody></speak>

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Near a base like 100, invoke Yavadunam — By the Deficiency! Lessen the number by its deficiency for the left part, then square the deficiency for the right part.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Observe: 94 is 6 below 100. Lessen 94 by 6 to get 88 on the left. Then square 6 to get 36 on the right. Put them together: 8836!</prosody></speak>

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Welcome to the universal key! Invoke Urdhva-Tiryagbhyam — Vertically and Crosswise! Three simple rays give the entire product in a single line.</prosody></speak>

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Watch: right vertical is 3 times 1 equals 3. Crosswise is 2 plus 12 equals 14: write 4, carry 1. Left vertical is 8 plus 1 equals 9. Combine them: 943!</prosody></speak>

english_meaning: If One is in Ratio, the Other is Zero

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, solving systems like 3x + 2y = 12 and 6x + 5y = 24 with elimination takes so many algebraic steps!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, solving simultaneous equations with elimination takes so many algebraic steps!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Spot the symmetry! Invoke Ānurūpye Śūnyamanyat — 'If One is in Ratio, the Other is Zero'! If the ratio of x-coefficients matches the constant ratio, the other variable y vanishes to zero!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Spot the symmetry! Invoke Anurupye Shunyamanyat — If One is in Ratio, the Other is Zero! When the x-ratio matches the constant ratio, y vanishes directly to zero.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Look closely: 3/6 = 12/24 = 1/2, so y = 0 immediately! Substitute y = 0 into 3x + 2(0) = 12: 3x = 12, so x = 4! The solution is x = 4, y = 0 without any elimination!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Look closely: 3 over 6 equals 12 over 24, so y is zero immediately! Then 3x equals 12, giving x equals 4 in one step!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now your turn, Shishya! In 2x + 3y = 8 and 4x + 7y = 16, the x-ratio (2/4) matches the constants (8/16), so y = 0. Solve for x: 2x = 8.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now your turn, Shishya! The x-ratio matches the constants, so y is zero. Solve for x: 2x equals 8!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, for 45x - 23y = 113 and 23x - 45y = 91, the numbers are huge! Cross-multiplying by 45 and 23 will take pages of messy algebra!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, for 45x minus 23y equals 113 and 23x minus 45y equals 91, the numbers are huge! Cross-multiplying will take pages of messy algebra!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Observe the cross-symmetry: the coefficients 45 and -23 interchange! Invoke Saṅkalana-Vyavakalanābhyām — 'By Addition and by Subtraction'! Simply add the equations once, and subtract them once, to reduce them to simple mental arithmetic!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Observe the cross-symmetry! The coefficients interchange. Invoke Sankalana-Vyavakalanabhyam — By Addition and by Subtraction! Simply add the equations once, and subtract them once, to reduce them to simple mental arithmetic.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Step 1 (Addition): Adding both equations gives 68x - 68y = 204. Divide by 68 to get x - y = 3! Step 2 (Subtraction): Subtracting Eq 2 from Eq 1 gives 22x + 22y = 22. Divide by 22 to get x + y = 1!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Step 1: Adding gives 68x minus 68y equals 204, so x minus y is 3! Step 2: Subtracting gives 22x plus 22y equals 22, so x plus y is 1!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now verify the subtraction step, Shishya! From 22x + 22y = 22, dividing both sides by 22 gives x + y. What is 22 ÷ 22?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now verify the subtraction step, Shishya! Dividing 22x plus 22y equals 22 by 22 gives x plus y. What is 22 divided by 22?</speak>

english_meaning: When the Collection is the Same, it is Zero

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, expanding 7(x + 1) = 8(x + 1) gives 7x + 7 = 8x + 8. Moving terms across the equals sign feels tedious when both sides share the exact same factor (x + 1)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, expanding 7 times x plus 1 equals 8 times x plus 1 feels tedious when both sides share the exact same factor!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Spot the common factor! Invoke Śūnyaṁ Sāmyasamuccaye — 'When the Collection is the Same, it is Zero'! When a shared factor appears on both sides with unequal multipliers, that common expression must vanish to zero!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Spot the common factor! Invoke Shunyam Samyasamuccaye — When the Collection is the Same, it is Zero! When a shared factor appears on both sides with unequal multipliers, that common expression must vanish to zero.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Subtract both sides: (7 - 8)(x + 1) = 0, giving -1(x + 1) = 0! Since -1 cannot be zero, the common factor must be zero: x + 1 = 0! Subtracting 1 yields x = -1 instantly, without expanding any brackets!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Subtracting both sides gives minus 1 times x plus 1 equals 0. Since minus 1 cannot be zero, x plus 1 must be zero, giving x equals minus 1 instantly!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now test your understanding, Shishya! In 7(x + 1) = 8(x + 1), since 7 ≠ 8, the common factor must equal zero: x + 1 = 0. Solve for x!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now test your understanding, Shishya! Since 7 does not equal 8, the common factor must equal zero: x plus 1 equals 0. Solve for x!</speak>

interactive_handshake.prompt_text: Solve for x: x + 1 = 0. Tap the value of x.

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji! In x² + 6x + 8 = 0, trial-and-error factoring is slow when numbers get large. How does Vedic math solve quadratics directly?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Guru-ji! In x squared plus 6x plus 8 equals 0, trial and error factoring is slow. How do we solve quadratics directly?</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Invoke Pūraṇāpūraṇābhyām — By Completion or Non-Completion! Move the constant to the right: x² + 6x = -8. Now complete the imperfect square on the left into a perfect square!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Invoke Puranapuranabhyam — By Completion or Non-Completion! Move constant 8 to the right: x squared plus 6x equals minus 8. Now complete the imperfect square on the left into a perfect square!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: To complete x² + 6x, take half of the x-coefficient: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, and square it: 3² = 9! Add 9 to both sides: x² + 6x + 9 = -8 + 9 ⟹ (x + 3)² = 1! Taking square roots yields x + 3 = ±1, giving roots x = -2 or x = -4!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Take half of 6, which is 3, and square it: 3 squared is 9! Adding 9 to both sides yields x plus 3 squared equals 1, giving roots minus 2 and minus 4!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now test your understanding, Shishya! In x² + 6x = -8, what completion term must you add to both sides to complete (x + 3)²? Calculate (6 ÷ 2)²!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now test your understanding, Shishya! To complete the square for x squared plus 6x, calculate 6 divided by 2 quantity squared!</speak>

english_meaning: Specific and General / Part and Whole

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji! Multiplying numbers like 58 × 62 requires full column calculation. Is there a way to solve it in our heads using symmetry?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Guru-ji! Multiplying numbers like 58 times 62 requires full column calculation. Can we solve it using symmetry?</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Invoke Vyaṣṭisamaṣṭiḥ — Part and Whole! 58 and 62 are symmetrically placed around their central whole average 60, with equal parts deviation of 2!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Invoke Vyashtisamashtih — Part and Whole! 58 and 62 are symmetrically placed around their whole average 60, with equal parts deviation of 2!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Apply the difference of squares: (A - d)(A + d) = A² - d²! The whole square is 60² = 3600. The parts square is 2² = 4. Subtract them: 3600 - 4 = 3596! Direct mental multiplication!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Square the whole: 60 squared is 3600. Square the parts deviation: 2 squared is 4. Subtract them: 3600 minus 4 equals 3596!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now test your understanding, Shishya! In 58 × 62, what is the central midpoint average of the two numbers: (58 + 62) ÷ 2?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now test your understanding, Shishya! In 58 times 62, what is the central midpoint average of the two numbers?</speak>

english_meaning: The Remainders by the Last Digit

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji! Converting fractions like 1/7 into exact repeating decimals takes long division with endless subtraction. Is there a faster Vedic shortcut?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Guru-ji! Converting fractions like 1 over 7 into repeating decimals takes long division. Is there a faster Vedic shortcut?</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Invoke Śeṣāṇyaṅkena Carameṇa — The Remainders by the Last Digit! Instead of long division, track only the remainder chain! Each remainder times 10 gives the next quotient digit and remainder.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Invoke Sheshanyankena Caramena — The Remainders by the Last Digit! Track the remainder chain: each remainder times 10 reveals the next digit and remainder!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Start with remainder 1: 10 ÷ 7 = 1 (R 3). Then 30 ÷ 7 = 4 (R 2). Then 20 ÷ 7 = 2 (R 6). The remainders 3 → 2 → 6 → 4 → 5 → 1 cycle back to 1, producing the 6-digit repetend 0.(142857)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Track the remainders: 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 1, repeating in 6 steps to give 0 point 1 4 2 8 5 7 repeating!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now test your understanding, Shishya! In step 3 with incoming remainder 2: 10 × 2 = 20. What is the new remainder: 20 mod 7?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now test your understanding, Shishya! In step 3, 10 times 2 is 20. What is the new remainder: 20 mod 7?</speak>

english_meaning: The Ultimate and Twice the Penultimate

dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji! Multiplying numbers like 143 by 12 takes tedious multi-line multiplication and endless adding. Is there a faster one-line Vedic secret?

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Invoke Sopāntyadvayamantyam — 'The Ultimate and Twice the Penultimate'! For multiplier 12, N = 2. Sandwich 143 with zero guards: 0 1 4 3 0. Pair each digit with N times its neighbor!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Invoke Sopantyadvayamantyam — The Ultimate and Twice the Penultimate! For multiplier 12, N is 2. Sandwich 143 with zero guards, then pair each digit with N times its neighbor!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU

english_meaning: The Product of the Sum is the Sum of the Products

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji! When factoring polynomials like (x + 3)(x + 2) = x² + 5x + 6, how can I quickly verify my answer without expanding every single term by hand?

dialogue_nodes.text: Invoke Guṇitasamuccayaḥ — 'The Product of the Sum is the Sum of the Products'! Evaluate at x = 1: the product of the factor coefficient sums must equal the sum of the polynomial's coefficients!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Invoke Gunitasamuccayah — The Product of the Sum is the Sum of the Products! Evaluate at x equals 1: the product of the factor sums must equal the sum of the product coefficients!</prosody></speak>

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Watch (x + 3)(x + 2): factor sums give 4 times 3 which is 12. The polynomial sum is 1 plus 5 plus 6, also 12! Both sums match 12, validating the factorization!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji! When factoring quadratics like x² + 7x + 10 = 0, how do I find the correct pair of numbers that multiply to 10 and add to 7?

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Invoke Guṇakasamuccayaḥ — 'The Factors of the Sum is the Sum of the Factors'! For x² + Bx + C = 0, seek factor pair (p, q) of constant C whose sum equals middle coefficient B: p · q = C and p + q = B!

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: For x² + 7x + 10 = 0, C = 10 and B = 7. Pairs of 10 are (1, 10) and (2, 5). Check sums: 1 + 10 = 11, but 2 + 5 = 7! So the factors are (x + 2)(x + 5) = 0, yielding roots x = −2 and x = −5!
